stimulus.body: 次の語について考えましょう：meat。

questions.stem: On a kanji chart, a single character is matched against possible meanings. Which gloss fits the kanji 肉 with on niku?

options.misconception: assigns a meaning belonging to another kanji, not 肉
assigns a meaning belonging to another kanji, not 肉
assigns a meaning belonging to another kanji, not 肉

questions.explanation: The kanji 肉 carries the meaning "meat" and is read niku in its Chinese-derived form. Knowing a kanji's core sense lets you build an approximate meaning for compounds even before you know every reading.
questions.hint: Think of the core idea represented by the character 肉.

questions.subject: JAPANESE
questions.learningObjective: identify the on-yomi of a kanji

stimulus.body: 次の語について考えましょう：bei。

questions.stem: What is the on-yomi reading of the kanji 米 meaning "rice"?

options.misconception: gives the reading of a different kanji rather than the on-yomi of 米
gives the reading of a different kanji rather than the on-yomi of 米
gives the reading of a different kanji rather than the on-yomi of 米

questions.explanation: The kanji 米, meaning "rice", has the on-yomi bei. The on-yomi is the reading borrowed from Chinese and is common in compound words, while the kun-yomi is the native Japanese reading used when the character stands alone.
questions.hint: Recall the Chinese-derived reading borrowed for the kanji 米.
